changes.name: Toxia
changes.entry:
Toxia is a country that poisoned itself and decided the poisoning was progress.

Once fertile, populous, and prosperous, Toxia became one of the world's great centers of chemistry during the Great Refinement. Its laboratories produced medicines, pigments, fertilizers, acids, preservatives, explosives, fuels, and industrial compounds in quantities previously unimaginable.

The factories brought extraordinary wealth.

They also killed the country.

Rivers changed color. Forests became stands of dead white timber. Aquifers filled with metals and chemical salts. Livestock were born malformed. Industrial towns disappeared beneath permanent yellow haze.

When the scale of the catastrophe finally became undeniable, Toxia faced a choice:

Destroy the industries upon which its economy depended—or learn to live in the poison.

Toxia chose the poison.

Today respirators are common clothing, children learn hazard symbols before they can properly read, and antidotes are kept beside household medicines. Toxian cities rise beneath forests of chimneys and elevated pipes. Warning sirens sound when the wind changes. Entire provinces can only be entered in protective equipment.

Toxians do not describe their homeland as ruined.

They describe it as adapted.

Capital: Contanima III

The capital of Toxia is Contanima III, an immense planned industrial city built after the loss of its two predecessors.

Nobody outside Toxia knows the complete truth about Contanima I and Contanima II.

Contanima I was gradually destroyed by contamination during the Great Refinement.

Official records state only that Contanima II was “retired following an unacceptable environmental event.”

Toxians rarely discuss it.

Contanima III was designed around the lessons of both disasters.

Not by polluting less.

By becoming better at surviving pollution.

Its districts are arranged according to prevailing winds. Administrative buildings have sealed ventilation systems. Chemical canals carry industrial waste through the city. Elevated pipelines form a second street system overhead.

An enormous contaminated canal connects Contanima III to the sea.

Nothing useful lives in its water.

Toxian submarines travel beneath it.

The Black Cabinet

Toxia is governed by the Black Cabinet, a council of nine senior officials responsible for the things considered essential to national survival: War, Chemistry, Medicine, Industry, Agriculture, Water, Trade, Intelligence, and Population.

The Cabinet meets around an enormous black glass table in Contanima III.

There are ten chairs.

Only nine are occupied.

No official explanation for the empty chair is given.

The head of the Black Cabinet is Dr. Malrec Vane, First Chair and ruler of Toxia.

Vane has governed for nearly thirty years. A physician and chemist by training, he is regarded within Toxia as one of the men responsible for saving the nation during the catastrophe at Contanima II.

Foreigners know him as the Black Physician.

Vane rarely speaks of morality.

He speaks of consequence.

His philosophy has become inseparable from modern Toxian government:

There are no harmless decisions.

Necessary Harm

Toxian government operates according to an unofficial principle known as Necessary Harm.

Every civilization causes suffering.

Toxia believes pretending otherwise is hypocrisy.

The responsibility of government is therefore not to avoid harm, but to calculate how much harm must be done in order to ensure national survival.

A village may be evacuated. A river may be sacrificed. A population may be exposed. A battlefield may be poisoned.

The question asked by the Black Cabinet is rarely:

“Is this wrong?”

It is:

“Is this necessary?”

The Pox Whisperers

The first Pox Whisperers were industrial physicians.

They entered contaminated factories, mines, chemical fires, epidemics, and poisoned neighborhoods when nobody else could.

Experienced Whisperers became capable of identifying toxins from minute signs: discoloration beneath a fingernail, a tremor, an unusual odor on the breath.

Workers claimed they could hear poison whispering inside a dying man.

The name remained.

During the 99 War, the profession became militarized.

Modern Pox Whisperers are part physician, part chemist, part battlefield engineer, and part executioner.

Their elaborate protective equipment may contain filters, antidotes, pressure tanks, analytical apparatus, poison reservoirs, sprayers, and the great brass chemical projectors commonly called Exhalers.

What emerges from an Exhaler depends entirely upon what its operator has loaded into it.

Pox Whisperers ultimately answer to the Black Cabinet.

The Toxian Navy

Toxia's surface navy is respectable but unremarkable.

Its submarine fleet is feared throughout the 99 War.

Toxian submarines do not rely upon ordinary combustion engines while submerged.

Instead they use sealed chemical reaction engines. Reactive compounds generate heat, pressure, or electrical current without requiring atmospheric oxygen.

This allows Toxian submarines to remain beneath the surface for unnervingly long periods.

Foreign sailors usually call them Vitriol Boats or Whisper Ships.

They are uncomfortable vessels: riveted hulls packed with ceramic reaction vessels, chemical tanks, valves, gauges, condensers, and miles of piping.

Even aboard ship, many crewmen wear respirators.

Leaks are common.

Veteran Toxian submariners can often be recognized by damaged voices, stained teeth, chemical burns, and permanently discolored fingertips.

A Whisper Ship does not necessarily need to attack another vessel. Some carry chemical shells. Others carry mines. Some carry enormous tanks.

A Toxian submarine can surface offshore on a favorable night, open a valve, and allow the wind to do the killing.

Toxia in the 99 War

Toxia is not trying to conquer the entire world.

It wants something more sustainable.

Dependence.

Toxia seeks control over the chemical industries upon which modern nations increasingly rely.

A kingdom may hate Toxia while still purchasing its medicines, fertilizers, preservatives, pesticides, industrial solvents, acids, chemical fuels, explosives, dyes, filtration systems, poisons, and antidotes.

Once a nation becomes dependent upon Toxian products, the Black Cabinet possesses a weapon that requires no army.

The Great Toxian Problem

Toxia's factories can supply half a continent.

Its homeland increasingly cannot supply the people running them.

The country desperately requires clean water, fertile soil, grain, meat, timber, livestock, seeds, medicinal plants, and uncontaminated territory.

Even clean earth is imported into Toxia.

Wealthy families maintain private gardens planted in foreign soil.

The Black Cabinet refers to fertile territory beyond Toxia's borders as Reserve Land.

Foreign governments have another word for it.

Conquest.

Trade

Major Exports

Toxia exports medicines, anesthetics, antiseptics, industrial chemicals, acids, solvents, fertilizers, pesticides, preservatives, dyes and pigments, chemical fuels, explosives, poisons, antidotes, respirators, filters, chemical engines, and specialized naval equipment.

Some Toxian medicines are genuinely among the finest in the world.

The factory producing an excellent treatment for poisoning may also manufacture the poison itself.

Toxians see no contradiction.

Major Imports

Toxia imports enormous quantities of food, grain, meat, clean water, livestock, timber, textiles, seeds, medicinal plants, uncontaminated soil, brass, copper, and glass.

Greatest Ally: Devor

Toxia's strongest major ally is Devor.

Their relationship is embodied in a collection of agreements known as the Ash Compact.

The alliance is entirely practical.

Toxia provides chemical expertise, industrial reagents, preservatives, corrosives, filtration compounds, medicines, and chemical weapons.

Devor provides heavy industry, machinery, military strength, energy, and access to conquered resources.

Neither trusts the other.

Both need the other.

Greatest Enemy: Veyr

Toxia's bitterest enemy is Veyr.

Veyr regards Toxian warfare as crude, indiscriminate, and fundamentally uncivilized.

Toxians consider that attitude ridiculous.

Veyr builds exquisite machines designed to tear human beings apart and then condemns Toxia because its weapons leave an unpleasant smell.

The rivalry became outright hatred after the Yellowing of Harrowgate.

The Yellowing of Harrowgate

A major Veyran position at Harrowgate was expected to withstand a siege lasting months.

Toxian artillery ended it in eleven minutes.

Hundreds of shells burst above the defenses and released a dense yellow-green cloud.

The vapor descended into streets, trenches, cellars, ventilation shafts, and shelters.

By sunset Harrowgate was almost silent.

Metal tarnished green. Birds fell from rooftops. Vegetation blackened. The wells remained dangerous for years.

The exact death toll remains unknown.

Toxian military histories call the event:

The Harrowgate Demonstration of Accelerated Siege Resolution.

Almost everyone else calls it:

The Yellowing.

It remains one of the most infamous actions of the 99 War.

Toxia and Fogport

Fogport's neutrality makes it exceptionally valuable to the Black Cabinet.

Toxian merchants openly sell medicines, disinfectants, dyes, industrial compounds, filters, pesticides, and agricultural chemicals throughout the city.

Their pharmacists have an unusual reputation.

A Toxian apothecary may save a man's life for three pennies.

The bottle beside the medicine may contain enough poison to kill everyone in the building.

Both will be carefully labeled.

Toxian merchants, naval officers, industrial agents, diplomats, spies, physicians, and Pox Whisperers regularly pass through Fogport.

Most claim to be there on business.

Usually they are telling the truth.

The difficulty is determining what kind of business.

Related

Dr. Malrec Vane · The Black Cabinet · Pox Whisperers · Contanima III · Devor · Veyr · The 99 War · Fogport

posts.name: Gamemaster Secrets
posts.entry:
Toxia Is Dying

The Black Cabinet has concealed the true extent of Toxia's ecological collapse.

The country does not have generations remaining.

It may have decades.

Aquifers thought to be protected are becoming contaminated. Agricultural districts maintained through heroic chemical intervention are beginning to fail.

The leadership knows this.

Toxia's increasingly aggressive behavior in the 99 War is therefore not simply imperial ambition.

They need another country.

Toxians Are Not Immune to Poison

Foreigners commonly believe generations of exposure have made Toxians extraordinarily resistant to toxins.

There is some truth to this, but nowhere near as much as Toxia encourages people to believe.

Much of the population depends upon an enormous government program of suppressants, mineral supplements, medicines, filtration systems, and low-dose antidotes known collectively as the Civic Regimen.

Millions of Toxians could become dangerously ill if those supplies stopped.

The Black Cabinet considers the composition of the Civic Regimen a state secret.

An enemy who discovered it could potentially cripple Toxia without firing a shot.

Fogport Plot Hooks

The Whisperer Who Won't Kill

A Pox Whisperer arrives in Fogport and immediately requests asylum.

He carries no military plans, troop movements, or secret treaties.

He carries a small black notebook containing the complete formulation of the Civic Regimen.

Toxia wants him returned. Veyr wants the notebook. Devor wants both destroyed.

The Whisperer claims he came to Fogport because the Collegium of Lumen is powerful enough to make the information public without immediately turning it into a weapon.

Unfortunately, he disappears before reaching it.

The Perfume Ship

A cargo vessel enters Fogport carrying several thousand ornate bottles of expensive Toxian perfume.

Then members of the dock crew begin collapsing.

The perfume is harmless.

The wooden crates are not.

The timber has been impregnated with a slow-release chemical compound—enough poison to contaminate several city blocks without importing a single suspicious container.

The question is not simply who brought it in.

Where are the other crates?

WHITE BREATH

Toxian chemists have discovered something astonishing about Fogport's famous fog.

Certain chemical aerosols bind to it.

Normally poison gas disperses.

Fogport's fog does not always behave normally.

A secret Toxian research group believes that with the correct compound, a poison released in one district could travel through the fog for hours—through alleys, open windows, sewers, ventilation shafts, and perhaps across much of the city.

The project is called WHITE BREATH.

Their experiments have already begun.

Small unexplained animal deaths around Fogport are the first evidence.

The Clean Garden

Hidden somewhere in Fogport is something more valuable to Toxia than Wychglass.

A garden.

A refugee horticulturist escaped Toxia carrying several dozen seeds from plant varieties believed extinct inside the country.

Some are food crops. Some are medicinal. Some can grow in heavily contaminated soil.

Toxian agents desperately want them back.

The horticulturist has no idea that one miserable-looking bean plant in her collection could potentially restore millions of acres of poisoned farmland.

The Antidote Man

Someone begins poisoning people throughout the Shambles.

The victims have nothing obvious in common.

Then a Toxian apothecary appears with an antidote that works perfectly.

Business becomes excellent.

The obvious explanation is that the apothecary is poisoning his own customers.

He isn't.

Someone else is conducting a market experiment to determine how quickly frightened civilians can be made dependent upon a proprietary Toxian medicine.

Fogport is merely the test market.

Eleven Minutes

A rusted Toxian artillery shell from the Yellowing of Harrowgate appears at an auction in Fogport.

It is supposedly empty.

Several governments want it. Veyr wants it destroyed. Toxia wants it returned. Collectors want it because it is one of the most infamous artifacts of the war.

Then someone discovers that the shell isn't empty.

It contains an intact sample of the original Harrowgate compound.

And the casing has begun to corrode.

A Pox Whisperer's House Call

A wealthy Fogport citizen discreetly hires the characters.

Someone has been poisoning him.

He has already hired physicians, alchemists, food tasters, and bodyguards. Nobody can determine how it is being done.

Finally he hires a Pox Whisperer.

The Whisperer studies the man's fingernails, smells his pillow, tastes the soot in his fireplace and announces:

“Nobody is poisoning you.”

Then he points toward the man's young daughter.

“They are poisoning her.”

The Exhaler

A Pox Whisperer's brass Exhaler turns up in a Nine Spoons pawnshop.

The owner has no idea what it is.

Neither did the thief who sold it.

The device contains six interchangeable chemical chambers.

Five are empty.

One isn't.

The original owner is searching for it.

So is Civic Vigilance.

And something inside the remaining chamber occasionally knocks against the glass.

The Bigger Campaign Secret

WHITE BREATH is not intended to destroy Fogport.

Toxia wants something much more useful.

They want to prove they could.

If Toxia can demonstrate that it possesses the ability to poison Fogport through its own fog, it can quietly threaten the one neutral city through which enormous portions of the 99 War's diplomacy, espionage, trade, contraband, refugees, and intelligence pass.

They would never need to conquer Fogport.

They could influence the entire war simply by keeping a finger on the valve.

That makes the Pox Whisperers in Fogport far more dangerous than ordinary assassins.

Most of them haven't come to kill anybody.

They've come to learn how the city breathes.

changes.name: Dr. Malrec Vane
changes.entry:
Dr. Malrec Vane is the First Chair of the Black Cabinet and ruler of Toxia.

He has governed the Poisoned Nation for nearly thirty years.

Vane is an elderly physician and chemist: tall, thin, impeccably groomed, and unfailingly courteous.

He rarely raises his voice.

He does not threaten.

He does not boast.

He does arithmetic.

Appearance

Vane dresses almost entirely in severe black clothing of exceptional quality.

The lower half of his face is concealed by a smooth black porcelain respirator.

Fine brass fittings disappear beneath his collar, and a narrow tube runs from the mask into the interior of his coat.

His lungs were permanently damaged during the catastrophe that destroyed Contanima II.

He cannot breathe normally without assistance.

Those who stand near him sometimes hear a faint wet bubbling beneath his clothing.

Nobody asks about it twice.

The First Chair

The Black Cabinet formally consists of nine equal members.

The First Chair theoretically possesses only one vote.

Nobody in Toxia believes that.

Vane dominates the Cabinet through reputation, intellect, political control, and an almost terrifying ability to reduce complex human disasters to measurable choices.

He does not regard himself as a dictator.

He considers himself the physician attending a critically ill nation.

Occasionally the treatment hurts.

Occasionally something must be amputated.

The Black Physician

Vane originally trained as a physician, toxicologist, and industrial chemist.

He became nationally famous during the disaster at Contanima II, where official histories credit him with directing emergency measures that saved enormous portions of the Toxian population.

His reputation propelled him into the Black Cabinet.

Within six years he became First Chair.

He has remained there ever since.

Among ordinary Toxians, Vane remains surprisingly popular.

He does not indulge in displays of wealth.

He visits industrial accidents personally.

He speaks with workers.

He remembers names.

He has stood inside contaminated hospitals alongside Pox Whisperers when safer officials remained miles away.

Many Toxians sincerely believe that Malrec Vane saved their country.

They may be correct.

Necessary Harm

Vane's political philosophy has shaped modern Toxia.

He believes that morality becomes increasingly difficult to apply as the number of lives involved increases.

A physician may refuse to sacrifice one innocent patient.

A ruler may discover that refusing to sacrifice one person condemns ten thousand others.

Vane therefore distrusts rulers who insist their hands are clean.

His most famous statement is:

“There are no harmless decisions.”

The doctrine now informally called Necessary Harm grew from his teachings.

Vane despises pointless cruelty.

He considers unnecessary suffering inefficient, vulgar, and morally indefensible.

The important word is unnecessary.

If forty thousand people must die to save four hundred thousand, Vane does not regard the decision as difficult.

He regards it as tragic.

Then he gives the order.

Personality

Vane is quiet, intelligent, patient, and remarkably pleasant company.

He listens carefully.

He asks excellent questions.

He is capable of genuine sympathy.

He prefers negotiation to violence and will work surprisingly hard to find a solution beneficial to everyone involved.

That is what makes meeting him dangerous.

When no mutually acceptable solution exists, Vane does not become angry.

He simply begins eliminating alternatives.

Eventually he asks:

“How many?”

The Pox Whisperers

Vane has an unusually close relationship with Toxia's Pox Whisperers.

They formally answer to the Black Cabinet, but the highest-ranking member of the order—the First Whisperer—reports directly to Vane.

Persistent rumors claim that Vane himself once served as a Pox Whisperer.

Official biographies neither confirm nor deny this.

He understands their techniques far too well for a conventional politician.

Veteran Whisperers address him with a small hand gesture rarely used by anyone else.

Foreign intelligence agencies have never determined what it means.

The Empty Chair

The Black Cabinet contains nine members.

Its chamber contains ten chairs.

The tenth is always empty.

Vane has never explained why.

Once, when a foreign ambassador jokingly asked whether Toxia was saving the chair for its next conquest, Vane reportedly looked toward the empty seat and replied:

“No. It is already occupied.”

He offered no further explanation.

Foreign Reputation

Outside Toxia, Malrec Vane inspires a strange mixture of fascination and horror.

He is not regarded as insane.

That would be considerably more comforting.

He is rational.

He understands exactly what Toxia's weapons do.

He understands the consequences of poisoned rivers, dead farmland, contaminated cities, and chemical warfare.

He simply believes that circumstances can exist in which all of those things are justified.

Veyran propaganda portrays him as a monster hiding behind a doctor's mask.

Devorian officials treat him with considerable respect.

Fogport's diplomats know him as one of the most dangerous men in the 99 War because Vane would rather purchase a port than invade it, compromise a minister rather than assassinate him, and make an enemy dependent upon Toxia rather than destroy him.

When violence becomes necessary, however, he has very few reservations about finishing the matter.

Related

Toxia · The Black Cabinet · Pox Whisperers · Contanima II · Contanima III · Devor · Veyr · Fogport · The 99 War

posts.name: Gamemaster Secrets
posts.entry:
Vane Destroyed Contanima II

Malrec Vane did save Toxia during the catastrophe at Contanima II.

The official histories simply omit how.

The contamination was not confined to factories or waterways.

Something had entered the population.

People leaving Contanima II were carrying it with them.

Vane calculated that if the evacuation continued, the contamination would spread into several of Toxia's remaining clean agricultural provinces.

Millions might eventually die.

So Dr. Malrec Vane ordered the evacuation stopped.

The gates were sealed. Bridges were destroyed. Rail lines were cut. Military units surrounded the city.

Hundreds of thousands of people remained inside.

Then Vane ordered Contanima II chemically sterilized.

The operation lasted three days.

There were virtually no survivors.

The epidemic ended.

Toxia survived.

Vane was celebrated for containing the disaster.

The public has never been told what containment meant.

Vane Still Has the Records

Every report from Contanima II was supposedly destroyed.

That is false.

Vane possesses a complete archive: medical reports, chemical analyses, population maps, orders, casualty estimates, letters from officials trapped inside the city, and transcripts of radio transmissions from civilians begging the government to reopen the gates.

The archive is known simply as:

BLACK TWO

Vane has never destroyed it.

Nobody knows why.

Perhaps guilt. Perhaps scientific value. Perhaps insurance. Perhaps Contanima II contained something the Black Cabinet expects to encounter again.

The Empty Chair

The tenth chair in the Black Cabinet belonged to Dr. Elian Sore, Vane's closest colleague during the Contanima II disaster.

Sore opposed sterilizing the city.

He insisted another treatment could be found.

Vane gave him several hours to prove it.

He failed.

Sore then refused evacuation and remained inside Contanima II with his patients.

Vane ordered the sterilization anyway.

The tenth chair has remained empty ever since.

Vane has never permitted anyone to remove it.

When he said “It is already occupied,” he meant it.

Vane Was a Pox Whisperer

Before entering government, Vane served for years as a field Pox Whisperer.

He was exceptionally good.

His specialty was not creating toxins.

It was determining exactly how much exposure a human body could survive.

Modern Toxian military doctrine concerning incapacitating doses, controlled exposure, antidote timing, and population-scale chemical attacks still incorporates calculations made by Vane decades ago.

Some of the Pox Whisperers regard him almost as the founder of their modern order.

Their private gesture toward him means:

We remember the dose.

Fogport Plot Hooks

BLACK TWO Comes to Fogport

Someone steals a portion of the Contanima II archive.

The thief flees to Fogport.

Suddenly everyone wants them.

Toxia wants the records returned. Veyr wants them published. Devor wants to know precisely what destroyed Contanima II. The Collegium wants the medical data.

Several people simply want proof that Malrec Vane murdered an entire city.

The stolen material contains something nobody expected:

Evidence that Vane may have been correct.

The Man Who Survived Contanima II

An elderly beggar appears in Nine Spoons.

He claims he escaped Contanima II after the gates were sealed.

Nobody believes him.

Then a visiting Pox Whisperer sees the man's scars.

The Whisperer goes completely pale.

Within hours, Toxian agents begin searching the district.

They do not seem interested in killing the old man.

They desperately want to know how he survived.

Vane Comes to Fogport

Malrec Vane visits Fogport personally.

That alone should frighten everyone.

The official purpose is trade negotiations.

The real reason is that WHITE BREATH has reached a stage Vane no longer trusts his own agents to oversee.

He wishes to inspect the project himself.

The player characters may find themselves protecting one of the most dangerous men alive because half the 99 War would like to murder him while he is standing on neutral ground.

Vane is an excellent temporary ally: polite, useful, extremely intelligent, and genuinely grateful when the characters save his life.

That does not mean he will abandon his plans.

The Black Physician Needs a Doctor

Vane's breathing apparatus begins failing while he is secretly in Fogport.

The replacement components are aboard a Toxian diplomatic vessel that cannot reach the city in time.

The only person capable of repairing the apparatus is someone Vane once condemned to death.

Now the characters must persuade that person to save him.

The patient himself refuses to threaten them.

He simply waits quietly while his breathing becomes worse.

Somebody Is Impersonating Vane

Orders bearing Vane's private authorization begin circulating among Toxian agents in Fogport.

They are genuine.

Vane did not issue them.

Someone has obtained access to a Black Cabinet cipher.

The orders instruct Pox Whisperers to begin preparing evacuation maps of Fogport.

Not invasion maps.

Evacuation maps.

Whoever issued them believes something is about to happen.

The Impossible Patient

A Pox Whisperer secretly approaches the characters.

He needs them to acquire a blood sample from someone inside Fogport.

He refuses to explain why.

The target turns out to be a perfectly healthy young woman whose mother fled Toxia decades ago.

Her blood contains markers associated with the contamination at Contanima II.

She was born years after the city died.

Whatever Vane tried to destroy may not have remained in Contanima II.

Vane's Greatest Fear

Malrec Vane is not afraid that history will call him a murderer.

He expects it to.

He is afraid that someday someone will prove that Contanima II did not need to die.

If Dr. Elian Sore was correct—if another treatment existed—then the central decision of Vane's life was not Necessary Harm.

It was merely harm.

That possibility frightens the Black Physician more than assassination, revolution, defeat, or death.
